A: **Demo vs Do-Check.** Demo: electrician narrates each fix. Do-Check: visitors fix. Each repair is logged with fault, failed tries, and trick used, building a visible failure wall so next table avoids repeats. Electrician picks next jobs for most new skill per minute, not queue order. Visitors work in threes: one opens, one checks stranger's work, one records. Example: toaster with dead cord teaches mains test reused on kettles. Test: after four Saturdays, give newcomers a never-seen lamp; if Do-Check group diagnoses live vs dead twice as often as Demo watchers, doing-plus-checking wins.
B: **Blast vs Baton.** Blast: both play lively all night. Baton: share crowd by clock. Agree 10-minute blocks on watches: holder plays chorus, dances, invites; yielder plays quiet drone below cap. Leadership passes automatically — no signals, slow side never waits past block. Number blocks sequentially so late starter knows whose turn holds after pause. Example: 7:00 North leads, South hushes; 7:10 swap. Test: count coins per half-hour at quiet end; if Baton quiet-end tips beat Blast quiet-end tips on matched Saturdays, yielding keeps both ends alive.
C: **Stack vs Ledger.** Stack: play tapes top-down. Ledger: log everything. Each drop gets numbered receipt copy; night's playlist is an appended log with tape numbers and minutes, posted on door, replayable to fix errors tomorrow by appending corrections not erasing. When tapes exceed three hours, drop order is fixed: repeats first, longest voices next, unplayed longest-waiting last to drop — never. Example: #47 plays 12:40-12:55 Tuesday; owner checks list Wednesday. Test: plant five 2-minute new voices; if all air within a week under Ledger vs two under Stack, queued fairness wins.
D: **Vault vs Weave.** Vault saves one grand girder in the new plaza by vote. Weave saves hundreds of small linked keepsakes. Each donor records a 30-second crossing memory tied to a specific rivet, cable cut, or paver — smallest worth linking — with when it happened and when recorded, so old stories aren't overwritten. Chosen cuts are stamped with their story codes and set into new railings. Example: runner's dawn-lap bolt #214 goes into mile-marker. Test: offer 20 anonymous replicas vs 20 storied cuts; if storied ones are claimed faster, lineage beats bigness.
